group.passage: Every year, people around the world throw away a huge amount of food. In 2022, the total was about 1.05 billion tonnes, and 60 percent of it came from homes. Below, two students tell us how their family and their school are trying to waste less food.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Mia: Clean the Fridge Night
passage_parts.text: Last spring, my mom put a list on our fridge. On it, she wrote down every food we threw away for a whole month: old bread, soft bananas, and half a pot of rice. When we read the list together, we were shocked. We were wasting food almost every day! So we made three simple rules. First, we check the fridge before we go shopping. Second, we cook smaller meals and save the extra food for lunch the next day. Third, we turn food that is getting old into something new. Soft bananas become banana bread, and old rice becomes fried rice. My little brother now calls Sunday "Clean the Fridge Night," and it is his favorite dinner of the week. Our list is much shorter now, and we spend less money on food, too.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Kevin: Taste First
passage_parts.text: At my school, the lunch line used to end at a big trash can. Many students took more food than they could eat, and the rest went straight into the can. This year, our student council started a plan called "Taste First." Before students fill their plates, they can try a small bite of each dish. If they do not like it, they simply skip it. The cooks also let us choose a small or a large bowl of rice. Every Friday, two students weigh the food that is left in the trash can and write the result on the wall. At first, many students did not care. After a few weeks, however, classes began to compete to waste the least. The cooks say they now prepare less food, and the trash can is much lighter than before.
